_README: One entry per service, driving the home page cards, /services, and the /services/<slug> pages via a single template. `tier: primary` shows as a headline card on the home page; `secondary` sits one level down. Slugs are keyword-bearing because they are the URL people search for — do not shorten them for tidiness. `notFor` is deliberate: saying who a service is wrong for converts better than claiming it suits everyone, and it filters the enquiries you don't want.

items.heading: Build a product
items.promise: A working, production-deployed product — not a prototype. Web app, API, infrastructure, CI, and a handover that lets your team take it over.
items.bestFor: Funded startups with a validated idea and no engineering team yet.

page.metaDescription: Trajectra builds production-ready web applications, APIs and infrastructure in 8–12 weeks, fixed scope and fixed price. Senior engineers on European hours.
page.lede: Most agencies hand back a prototype and call it an MVP. We deploy a product your customers can use and your team can maintain — with the infrastructure, tests and documentation that makes the second release as fast as the first.
includes: Discovery and scoping, ending in a written specification you own
Web application, API and database, built to your requirements
Cloud infrastructure, CI/CD and environment setup
Automated tests covering the paths that would cost you money if they broke
Weekly demos against working software, in your repository
Documentation, runbooks and a walkthrough with whoever takes it on
notFor: Ideas that have not been validated with anyone who would pay for them. Build it yourself in no-code first, then come back.
Projects that need to start next week. Our lead time is usually 2–4 weeks.
Anyone looking for the cheapest possible quote. We are not it, and we will say so on the call.

faq.q: What if the scope changes mid-build?
faq.a: It usually does. Changes go through a written change order with a revised price and date before any work starts, so the number never moves without you agreeing to it first.

faq.q: What stack do you build in?
faq.a: Typically TypeScript across the board — React or Next.js on the front end, Node on the back — with Postgres and a managed cloud platform. We will use something else if your team already runs it; the goal is a codebase you can hire for, not one we enjoyed writing.

faq.q: Do we get the code if we stop?
faq.a: Yes, unconditionally. It is in your repository from the first commit and the IP is yours on payment for work completed.

items.heading: Modernise what you have
items.promise: Legacy systems brought up to date without a rewrite you can't afford. Framework upgrades, cloud migration, performance work, and the test coverage that makes the next change safe.
items.bestFor: Teams whose codebase has become the reason releases are slow.

page.metaDescription: Framework upgrades, cloud migration and performance work on systems you cannot afford to rewrite. Starts with a two-week assessment and a costed plan.
page.lede: The instinct with an ageing codebase is to rewrite it. That is almost always the most expensive option and the one most likely to fail. We start by finding out whether it is actually necessary — and usually it is not.
includes: Two-week assessment: architecture, dependencies, security, test coverage, delivery bottlenecks
A written rewrite-versus-refactor recommendation, with the reasoning shown
A remediation plan ordered by risk and cost, not by what is most interesting
Framework and dependency upgrades, executed incrementally so you keep shipping
Cloud migration and infrastructure-as-code where it pays for itself
Test coverage added around the parts that change most often
notFor: Anyone who has already decided on a full rewrite and wants someone to execute it. We will argue with you, which is not what you are buying.
Systems nobody in your organisation can explain and nobody has documentation for. That is an archaeology project first — we can do that, but it is scoped separately.
Codebases that are genuinely fine and merely unfashionable.

faq.q: Can you work on a stack you don't normally use?
faq.a: For the assessment, usually yes — architecture, dependency risk and delivery bottlenecks are largely language-independent. For the remediation itself we will tell you honestly whether we are the right team or whether you need a specialist.

The assessment exists partly to find out where breakage would hurt most, and coverage goes in there first. Upgrades ship incrementally behind your existing release process rather than as one large merge.

faq.q: What if the assessment says we should rewrite?
faq.a: Then it says so, with the costs of both routes laid out. You are not obliged to do the rewrite with us, and the plan is yours regardless.

items.heading: Embed a team
items.promise: Senior engineers working inside your process — your standups, your board, your repository. Not a black box you brief and wait on.
items.bestFor: Product teams that need to move faster than they can hire.

page.metaDescription: Senior engineers embedded in your team, in your process and your repository, on European hours. Monthly, three-month minimum, thirty-day exit.
page.lede: Hiring a senior engineer in London or Berlin takes three to six months and often fails twice before it works. Embedding is not a permanent substitute for that — it is what keeps the roadmap moving while you do it.
includes: Named engineers, not a rotating pool — you know who is on your work
In your standups, your issue tracker and your repository from day one
Working to your definition of done and your review standards
Four hours of live overlap with London, six with New York, all day with Europe
Monthly billing per engineer, three-month minimum, thirty days' notice to stop
notFor: Teams with no technical lead to set direction. Embedded engineers amplify a roadmap; they cannot invent one.
Work that needs someone in the room. Some things genuinely do.
Anyone wanting to bill by the hour. We price by the month so nobody is counting minutes.

faq.q: How is this different from hiring a freelancer?
faq.a: Continuity and cover. Engineers work as a team with shared context, so a holiday or an illness does not stop your roadmap, and the knowledge does not leave when one person does.
Talk to us. We would rather have that conversation openly than pretend it never comes up — but it is a conversation, not an automatic right, and there is a fee.
Thirty days' notice, no penalty. If it is not working in month one we would rather know in month one.

items.heading: Technical training
items.promise: Hands-on workshops in React, Node, cloud architecture and system design, run against your own codebase rather than a toy example.

page.metaDescription: Hands-on workshops in React, Node, cloud architecture and system design, run against your own codebase rather than a generic example project.
page.lede: Most corporate training teaches a framework against an example app nobody will ever ship. We run sessions against your codebase, on the problems your team actually has this quarter.
includes: Workshops in React and Next.js, Node and API design, cloud architecture, testing, and system design
Delivered against your repository and your real constraints
Live and remote, in your working hours
Written materials and recordings your team keeps
Follow-up session a month later, when the questions have actually surfaced
notFor: Certification programmes. We do not issue them and would not want to.
Teams looking to tick a professional-development box. It will be obvious to everyone involved.

faq.q: How large can a group be?
faq.a: Six to twelve works best. Beyond that it becomes a lecture, which is a worse format for anything hands-on.
Yes — sessions for product managers and founders on how to scope technical work and read a technical proposal tend to pay for themselves quickly.

items.heading: IT & technology advisory
items.promise: Architecture reviews, vendor selection, and technical due diligence for teams making a decision they can't easily reverse.

page.metaDescription: Architecture reviews, vendor selection and technical due diligence for teams making decisions that are expensive to reverse.
page.lede: Some technical decisions are cheap to change later. Others set your cost base and hiring profile for years. This is for the second kind.
includes: Architecture and infrastructure review with a written recommendation
Build-versus-buy analysis with the operating costs of both
Vendor and platform selection, including the questions to ask that vendors dislike
Technical due diligence on a codebase you are about to acquire or invest in
A named engineer available for the follow-up questions, not just the report
notFor: Decisions already made that need external validation. We will probably give you the wrong answer.
Ongoing fractional-CTO cover — that is a different engagement, and often a different person.

faq.q: Do you recommend your own delivery services in the report?
faq.a: If the honest answer is that you should build something, the report says so — but the recommendation and the quote are separate documents, and you are under no obligation to use us for either.

faq.q: How quickly can you turn around due diligence?
faq.a: A focused codebase review is usually one to two weeks depending on size and access. Tell us the deadline on the call.

items.heading: Network design & security
items.promise: Network architecture, infrastructure hardening and connectivity for organisations with on-premise requirements.

page.metaDescription: Network architecture, infrastructure hardening and connectivity for organisations with on-premise or hybrid requirements.
page.lede: Not everything moves to the cloud. For organisations with on-premise or hybrid requirements — regulatory, latency, or simply existing investment — the network is still the foundation everything else sits on.
includes: Network architecture and segmentation design
Infrastructure hardening and access control review
Connectivity and capacity planning across sites
Documentation your own team can operate from
notFor: Organisations that are fully cloud-native. Your equivalent problems live in your cloud configuration, and that is the advisory engagement instead.
Emergency incident response. We are not a 24/7 operations desk.

faq.q: Is this mainly a Nigeria service?
faq.a: In practice yes — work with a physical component needs people on site, and our engineers are in Lagos. Software engagements are remote worldwide.
